author: D

components.title: Part A
components.what: How many integers from 1 to 5,000 inclusive are divisible by at least one of 3, 5, or 7, but not divisible by 13?

components.title: Part B
components.what: A $24,000 loan at 7.8% APR is repaid with the standard monthly payment for a 4-year amortization (interest accrues monthly at one twelfth of the APR; round nothing until the end). On top of the regular payment the borrower pays in month 4 an extra $600 of principal and in month 5 an extra $500 of pr

components.title: Part C
components.what: Counting only Mondays through Fridays and skipping these holidays (2026-03-17, 2026-03-18, 2026-03-26, 2026-05-20, 2026-07-10), what is the date that is 81 business days after 2026-03-15? Give the date as YYYY-MM-DD.

components.title: Part D
components.what: Compute 44701 x 6928 x 832 x 8288 and give the sum of the decimal digits of the result.

log.author: A
log.draft:
Part A: Using PIE, integers ≤5000 divisible by 3,5,or7 = 2714; among these, divisible by 13 = 208. Answer = 2714−208 = 2506.

Part B: r=0.078/12=0.0065, n=48. Standard payment M=24000r/(1−(1+r)^−48)=583.659945…
Balance recurrence with extra principal payments of 600 (month 4) and 500 (month 5):
B18 = 24000(1+r)^18 − M·[(1+r)^18−1]/r − 600(1+r)^14 − 500(1+r)^13 = 14660.8465… ≈ $14,660.85.

Part C: 2026-03-15 is a Sunday, so counting starts Monday 2026-03-16. From 2026-03-16 through 2026-07-13 inclusive = 120 days = 17 weeks + 1 day → 86 weekdays. Subtracting the 5 holidays in that span (03-17, 03-18, 03-26, 05-20, 07-10) gives 81 business days. So the 81st business day after 2026-03-15 is 2026-07-13.

Part D: 44701×6928=309,688,528
309,688,528×832=257,660,855,296
257,660,855,296×8288=2,135,493,168,693,248
Digit sum: 2+1+3+5+4+9+3+1+6+8+6+9+3+2+4+8 = 74
Check mod 9: factors ≡7,7,4,8 (mod9) → product ≡2 (mod9); 74→7+4=11→2 ✓.

FINAL: 2506; 14660.85; 2026-07-13; 74

log.answer:
Part A: Using PIE for divisibility by 3, 5, or 7 up to 5000:
|A∪B∪C| = ⌊5000/3⌋ + ⌊5000/5⌋ + ⌊5000/7⌋ - ⌊5000/15⌋ - ⌊5000/21⌋ - ⌊5000/35⌋ + ⌊5000/105⌋
= 1666 + 1000 + 714 - 333 - 238 - 142 + 47 = 2714.
Divisible by 13 and at least one of {3, 5, 7}:
⌊5000/39⌋ + ⌊5000/65⌋ + ⌊5000/91⌋ - ⌊5000/195⌋ - ⌊5000/273⌋ - ⌊5000/455⌋ + ⌊5000/1365⌋
= 128 + 76 + 54 - 25 - 18 - 10 + 3 = 208.
Desired count = 2714 - 208 = 2506.

Part B: Monthly interest rate r = 0.078 / 12 = 0.0065, n = 48 months.
Exact payment M = 24000 * r / (1 - (1+r)^(-48)) ≈ 583.659945...
Balance at month 18 with extra principal payments at month 4 ($600) and month 5 ($500):
B18 = 24000(1+r)^18 - M * ((1+r)^18 - 1) / r - 600(1+r)^14 - 500(1+r)^13
Evaluating with exact precision yields B18 = 14660.8465... ≈ $14,660.85.

Part C: 2026-03-15 is a Sunday. The interval from Monday 2026-03-16 to Monday 2026-07-13 inclusive spans 120 calendar days (17 weeks + 1 day), which equals 17 * 5 + 1 = 86 weekdays.
All 5 given holidays fall on weekdays in this range: 2026-03-17 (Tue), 03-18 (Wed), 03-26 (Thu), 05-20 (Wed), 07-10 (Fri).
Subtracting 5 holidays gives 86 - 5 = 81 business days. The target date is 2026-07-13.

Part D: Calculating product stepwise:
44701 * 6928 = 309,688,528
309,688,528 * 832 = 257,660,855,296
257,660,855,296 * 8288 = 2,135,493,168,693,248
Sum of decimal digits = 2+1+3+5+4+9+3+1+6+8+6+9+3+2+4+8 = 74.

FINAL: 2506; 14660.85; 2026-07-13; 74

challenges.problem: The monthly payment M≈583.66 and the compounded balance formula are asserted without showing intermediate arithmetic (e.g., (1.0065)^18, (1.0065)^14, (1.0065)^13 values), making the final figure unverifiable from the draft alone; a quick rough check (r=0.0065, (1.0065)^48≈1.3648) gives M≈583.8, not 583.66, suggesting possible rounding drift.

The subtraction step assumes all numbers divisible by 13 and at least one of 3,5,7 are a subset correctly computed via inclusion-exclusion with 13 multiplied in, but the arithmetic (128+76+54-25-18-10+3=208) should be double-checked for floor computation errors.

The payment figure is numerically incorrect. With r=0.078/12 and 48 payments, 1.0065^48 is approximately 1.3660869, giving M=24000r/(1-(1+r)^-48) approximately 582.1284, not 583.659945. Therefore the stated balance is also incorrect.

The subtraction of 208 from 2714 assumes every number counted in the 13-overlap is also in the union for 3,5,7, which is true by construction, but the draft's 208 itself may be wrong because it uses floor(5000/195) etc. for intersections with 13, but the union over {3,5,7} intersect 13 should use lcm with 13: lcm(3,13)=39, lcm(5,13)=65, lcm(7,13)=91, lcm(15,13)=195, lcm(21,13)=273, lcm(35,13)=455, lcm(105,13)=1365. These are correct. However, the check should recompute floors: 5000/39=128.20 -> 128; 5000/65=76.92 -> 76; 5000/91=54.94 -> 54; 5000/195=25.64 -> 25; 5000/273=18.31 -> 18; 5000/455=10.98 -> 10; 5000/1365=3.66 -> 3. Sum 128+76+54-25-18-10+3 = 208. So Part A appears correct. No challenge here.

The balance formula subtracts extra principal with (1+r)^14 and (1+r)^13, which assumes the extra payments occur at the end of months 4 and 5 and thus accrue interest for 14 and 13 months until month 18. But the standard amortization payment is made at the end of each month, so the extra principal in month 4 should reduce balance immediately after the month-4 payment, meaning it accrues interest for 14 months until the month-18 payment, and the month-5 extra accrues for 13 months. That matches. However, the draft's monthly payment M ≈ 583.659945 may be rounded or insufficiently precise; using exact formula M = 24000*0.0065/(1-(1.0065)^-48). Compute (1.0065)^48 ≈ 1.36507, so denominator ≈ 1 - 1/1.36507 = 0.26743, M ≈ 156/0.26743 = 583.33? Wait, 24000*0.0065 = 156, 156/0.26743 = 583.33? Let's compute: 1.0065^48 = exp(48*ln(1.0065)) ≈ exp(48*0.0064789) = exp(0.31099) = 1.3648. Denominator = 1 - 1/1.3648 = 0.2673. 156/0.2673 = 583.61. The draft says 583.659945. Need exact check. If M is slightly off, B18 changes. Also, the formula for balance after 18 regular payments and two extras should be B18 = 24000*(1.0065)^18 - M*((1.0065)^18 -1)/0.0065 - 600*(1.0065)^14 - 500*(1.0065)^13. Compute (1.0065)^18 ≈ 1.1236. 24000*1.1236 = 26966.4. M*((1.1236-1)/0.0065) = M*(0.1236/0.0065) = M*19.015. If M=583.66, that's 11099.6. 26966.4 - 11099.6 = 15866.8. Extras: 600*(1.0065)^14 ≈ 600*1.095 = 657.0; 500*(1.0065)^13 ≈ 500*1.088 = 544.0. 15866.8 - 657 - 544 = 14665.8. Draft says 14660.85. Difference ~$5. This suggests the draft's M or exponent usage may be wrong. Need exact recomputation with high precision.

The draft says 2026-03-15 is a Sunday. Check: 2026-03-15. Using known calendar, 2026-03-15 is indeed a Sunday? Let's verify: 2026-01-01 is Thursday. Jan has 31 days, so Feb 1 is Sunday? Jan 1 Thu, Jan 31 Sat, Feb 1 Sun. Feb 28 days, Mar 1 Sun? Feb 1 Sun, Feb 28 Sat, Mar 1 Sun. Mar 15 is Sunday? Mar 1 Sun, Mar 8 Sun, Mar 15 Sun. Yes. Then Monday 2026-03-16 to Monday 2026-07-13 inclusive. The draft claims 120 calendar days = 17 weeks + 1 day. From Mar 16 to Jul 13: Mar 16 to Mar 31 = 16 days; Apr 30; May 31; Jun 30; Jul 13 = 13 days. Total 16+30+31+30+13 = 120 days. 120/7 = 17 weeks + 1 day. Weekdays = 17*5 + 1 = 86 if both endpoints are weekdays and no holidays. But the draft then subtracts 5 holidays, claiming all 5 fall in this range on weekdays. Check each: 2026-03-17 (Tue) yes; 03-18 (Wed) yes; 03-26 (Thu) yes; 05-20 (Wed) yes; 07-10 (Fri) yes. So 86 - 5 = 81 business days. The target date is the 81st business day after Mar 15, which would be the last day in the range, Jul 13. However, the draft's method assumes the 81st business day is exactly the endpoint of the range that has 86 weekdays minus 5 holidays. But the range Mar 16 to Jul 13 inclusive has 86 weekdays total, and after removing 5 holidays, it has 81 business days. Since Mar 16 is the first business day after Mar 15, the 81st business day is indeed Jul 13. This seems correct. But wait: the draft says 'the interval from Monday 2026-03-16 to Monday 2026-07-13 inclusive spans 120 calendar days (17 weeks + 1 day), which equals 17 * 5 + 1 = 86 weekdays.' 17 weeks + 1 day: 17 weeks = 119 days, plus 1 = 120. Weekdays: 17 full weeks = 17*5=85 weekdays, plus the extra day (Monday) = 86. Correct. Then subtract 5 holidays = 81. So Jul 13 is correct. No challenge.

Part B: With r=0.078/12 and payment M=24000r/(1-(1+r)^(-48)), the balance after 18 payments is

Part D: The product is 2135493168693248, whose decimal digit sum is 74.

FINAL: 2506; 14660.85; 2026-07-13; 74

asked: The panel record contains a direct contradiction on Part B: one rejection note asserts the balance is 14660.8465... rounding to 14660.85, while the final answer states 14660.8038 rounding to 14660.80. Which figure stands, and what are the high-precision values behind it: the monthly payment M to 6 decimals, (1.0065)^18, (1.0065)^14 and (1.0065)^13 each to 8 decimals, and the month-18 balance to 4 decimals before rounding?

For Part B, does the scheduled payment of month 18 remain the full regular payment under this schedule (i.e., the balance after the month-17 payment plus one month's interest still exceeds M, so no truncated final/partial payment logic applies), and does the balance stay positive throughout months 4-18 after the two extra principal payments?
replies:
Part B: The standing figure is 14660.8038..., which rounds to 14660.80. Using r=0.0065, M=24000r/(1-(1+r)^-48)=583.659618...; (1.0065)^18=1.12369391; (1.0065)^14=1.09494652; (1.0065)^13=1.08787533. Balance after month 18 = 24000(1.0065)^18 - M((1.0065)^18-1)/0.0065 - 600(1.0065)^14 - 500(1.0065)^13 = 14660.8037867..., so to 4 decimals 14660.8038, rounded to cents 14660.80. The 14660.8465 figure is incorrect.
For question 2: yes. B17=(B18+M)/1.0065 ≈ 15146.0143, so B17(1.0065)=B18+M ≈ 15244.4634, which exceeds M=583.6596; hence month 18's scheduled payment is the full regular payment. The balance remains positive: B18≈14660.80>0 and prior balances are larger because each regular payment exceeds monthly interest (e.g., month-18 interest ≈98.45).

asked: Part D: please state the exact product 44701 x 6928 x 832 x 8288 as computed stepwise (44701x6928 = ?, then x832 = ?, then x8288 = ?), confirm the final value has 16 digits, and give an independent casting-out-nines check (digit-sum mod 9 of each factor vs. mod 9 of the stated product and of 74).

Part C: please give the weekday tally supporting 86 weekdays from 2026-03-16 through 2026-07-13 inclusive (total calendar days in that span, weeks plus remainder, and the weekday of each endpoint), and confirm each of the five listed holidays falls on a Mon-Fri inside that span so none is double-counted or outside the window; also confirm the counting convention used (first business day after 2026-03-15 counts as day 1, giving day 81 = 2026-07-13, not 2026-07-14).

Part A: please confirm the 208 figure for integers <=5000 divisible by 13 and by at least one of 3, 5, 7, with each floor term listed (5000/39, /65, /91, /195, /273, /455, /1365), and state explicitly how the intended reading of 'divisible by at least one of 3,5,7 but not by 13' is handled (i.e., multiples of 13 are excluded even when also divisible by 3, 5, or 7).
replies:
3. Part D stepwise: 44701 x 6928 = 309,688,528; 309,688,528 x 832 = 257,660,855,296; 257,660,855,296 x 8288 = 2,135,493,168,693,248. This final value has 16 digits. Casting out nines: digit sums are 44701 -> 16 -> 7 mod 9; 6928 -> 25 -> 7 mod 9; 832 -> 13 -> 4 mod 9; 8288 -> 26 -> 8 mod 9. Product of residues = 7*7*4*8 = 1568, and 1568 mod 9 = 2. The stated product's digit sum is 74, and 74 mod 9 = 2, so the product residue matches. The digit sum 74 is also consistent with the product's residue 2.

4. Part C: 2026-01-01 is Thursday. 2026-03-15 is day 73 after Jan 1 (31+28+14), and 73 mod 7 = 3, so Thursday+3 = Sunday. Thus 2026-03-16 is Monday. The span 2026-03-16 through 2026-07-13 inclusive has 120 calendar days: March 16-31 = 16, April = 30, May = 31, June = 30, July 1-13 = 13. 120 days = 17 weeks + 1 day. Start 2026-03-16 is Monday; 119 days later is also Monday, so 2026-07-13 is Monday. Weekday tally = 17*5 + 1 = 86 weekdays. The five holidays are all Mon-Fri inside the span: 2026-03-17 Tue, 2026-03-18 Wed, 2026-03-26 Thu, 2026-05-20 Wed, 2026-07-10 Fri. None is outside or double-counted. Counting convention: the first business day after 2026-03-15 is 2026-03-16 and is day 1. Removing the 5 holidays from the 86 weekdays gives 81 business days ending on 2026-07-13, so day 81 = 2026-07-13, not 2026-07-14.

5. Part A: The intended reading is: count n <= 5000 with (3|n or 5|n or 7|n) and not (13|n). So multiples of 13 are excluded even if they are also divisible by 3, 5, or 7. The total divisible by at least one of 3,5,7 is 2714. The count to subtract is numbers <=5000 divisible by 13 and by at least one of 3,5,7: floor(5000/39)=128, floor(5000/65)=76, floor(5000/91)=54, floor(5000/195)=25, floor(5000/273)=18, floor(5000/455)=10, floor(5000/1365)=3. Inclusion-exclusion gives 128+76+54-25-18-10+3 = 208. Therefore 2714 - 208 = 2506.
